description: hugoh/hk-config//renovate.json is extended (through presets/base) so every consumer gets its custom managers (the hugoh/hk-config and jdx/hk pins in *.pkl / mise.toml) and its global disable of the built-in mise manager for `hk`. Repos with no hk.pkl are unaffected — those managers just match nothing. Since ~every repo uses hk.pkl, this is injected in the base rather than opted into per repo. The timezone, 7-day soak, monthly window and vulnerability alerts also come from presets/base.

packageRules.description: config:best-practices pulls in security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, whose packageRule lowers npm to 3 days and would otherwise override the top-level 7 days.

My own packages (actions, reusable workflows, spoons, ...) don't need the 7-day soak meant for third-party supply-chain risk: 1 day is enough to catch a bad release. Must stay above the first-party gh-workflows rule below so its 12-hour override still wins in the repos it covers.

My own packages get their own group instead of the generic "minor updates"/"patch updates" ones: a group takes its schedule from the generic rule that grouped it, so without this a consumer's hugoh/** schedule override (e.g. daily) is ignored for any update that lands in a generic group. Majors stay ungrouped, as for third-party packages. Must stay BELOW the generic minor/patch rules (their groupName would replace it) and ABOVE the first-party core rule below, whose groupName must win.

hk and hk-config are linter infrastructure: a release can add or change checks and fail CI, and hk-config needs a minimum hk version, so they move together in the one linters PR and its first-weekend window. The pins are read by custom managers (hk.pkl, mise.toml) and the built-in mise manager is disabled for hk, so the linters rule above, which is limited to the mise manager and mise.toml, never sees them: same groupName, separate rule. Not in the hk-config repo itself, where hk is an integral part of the project rather than a tool it lints with; there hk stays in the generic groups. The github-actions manager's hk-config usage is the first-party core rule below.

First-party reusable workflows and composite actions: a bump only reaches consumers once a new tag is cut, so propagate within a day and automerge. Restricted to the repos that own these workflows/actions. Needs its own groupName so it isn't swallowed into the "minor updates"/"patch updates" groups above, which would otherwise pull in their monthly/weekly schedules instead of "at any time".

Linters pinned in the repo's own mise.toml move together on the first weekend of the month: a linter release that adds a rule can fail CI, so batching them keeps that to one PR and keeps it from blocking the weekly groups. The list is the tools behind hk-config's base.pkl steps (its stepTools, checked by scripts/check-package-rules.mjs, which fails on a tool that is neither listed here nor excluded there) plus editorconfig-checker. biome and npm:renovate keep their own groups below, and tofu/trivy stay weekly. Only the repo-root mise.toml: global tool files and mise.ci.toml keep the weekly groups. Needs its own groupName (a group with mixed schedules falls back to the wrong one) and must stay BELOW the generic minor/patch rules, which would otherwise replace it, and ABOVE biome toolchain.

The renovate CLI ships several times a day: its own group and the Saturday-early window. presets/npm-renovate-debounce says the same for go-tools, but its rule comes before the generic minor/patch rules above, which replace both group and schedule, so it has to be repeated here (a rule can't extend a preset that holds packageRules).

The biome toolchain group: the CLI pin in mise.toml and the $schema URL in biome.json (read by customManagers:biomeVersions) are read by different managers, so group them to move in ONE PR and keep the CLI from lagging the schema it validates against (biome warns when they differ). Both are looked up on npm: the mise manager's own github-tags lookup finds no biome updates (the tags are named @biomejs/biome@<version>), so without the override the CLI pin never moved. First-weekend-of-the-month window like the linters: biome is a linter and formatter, and a release that adds a rule or changes the formatting can fail CI. Must stay BELOW the generic minor/patch grouping rules above, or their groupName replaces it (later packageRules win); scripts/check-package-rules.mjs enforces it.
